api/index.ts.//: The Nest application is compiled ahead of time by `nest build`; the entry point only loads it. `includeFiles` is what carries that output and the Prisma query engine into the lambda — Vercel's dependency tracing follows static imports, and both are reached dynamically.
api/index.ts.//maxDuration: A cold start pays for Nest construction plus a Neon compute wake. 30s is the ceiling, not the budget — NFR-PER-003 still expects 600ms at P95 once warm.

//rewrites: Every path goes to the one function; Nest's router decides what it is. The API is versioned by path prefix (COM-002), so /api/v1/... arrives intact.
//crons: §5.3: the daily billing pass — mark instalments due and overdue, send the FR-PAY-019 notices, then freeze anything past its grace period. A serverless function has no timer, so Vercel Cron drives it. 05:00 UTC is 06:00 Africa/Douala: early enough that a payer who acts on the notice has the whole working day, late enough not to send an SMS at midnight. Vercel authenticates the call with CRON_SECRET; the endpoint refuses without it.

env.//CC_DISABLE_SCHEDULERS: Belt and braces. BillingSchedulerService already refuses to start a timer when it detects a serverless runtime; this states the intent in the deployment configuration too, where an operator reading it can see why.
